title: Project: Persistent Notes Manager
learningObjectives: Create and append notes using Java file APIs and explicit UTF-8
Read saved text safely and list notes in the application directory
Handle missing files and invalid paths with clear error messages
Close file resources reliably when operations succeed or fail
Verify persisted notes using Unicode and repeated application runs

understand.concept: Persist text between runs using an application-owned directory, UTF-8 encoding and try-with-resources. Treat file paths as data to validate.
understand.whyItMatters: Project: Persistent Notes Manager helps learners create Java applications that are easier to reason about, test and maintain.
understand.analogy: Treat the concept as a clearly labeled tool for one programming responsibility.
understand.analogyLimit: Actual behavior is defined by Java language rules and API contracts.

explain.narrative:
## Project purpose and storage design

Build a notes manager that creates, lists, appends to and deletes text notes across application runs. Choose an application-owned data directory rather than accepting arbitrary paths from untrusted input. Decide how a note is identified (for example, a validated ID mapped to a file name) and keep that mapping separate from the note's displayed title.

## Use explicit text encoding and safe file APIs

Use `Files.writeString`, `Files.readString` or a buffered reader/writer with `StandardCharsets.UTF_8`. Specify whether a save replaces existing content or appends to it; these are different operations and should be visible in method names. Use try-with-resources for streams and writers. Validate note IDs and resolve paths against the chosen storage directory so a user cannot escape it with path traversal such as `../`.

## Handle missing files and partial failures

A list operation should handle an empty notes directory. Reading a missing note should produce a clear “not found” result rather than an unexplained stack trace. Report I/O failures without claiming a save succeeded. For a robust update, write the new content to a temporary file and replace the target only after the write completes successfully.

## Verify persistence and cleanup

Test Unicode text, an empty note, append behavior, a missing ID, invalid IDs and an I/O failure. Restart the application and confirm saved content remains. Clean up temporary test files even when an operation fails, and avoid deleting files outside the application's own data directory.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.nio.file.Path p = java.nio.file.Files.createTempFile("note", ".txt"); try { java.nio.file.Files.writeString(p, "Hello", java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8); System.out.println(java.nio.file.Files.readString(p)); } finally { java.nio.file.Files.deleteIfExists(p); } } }
examples.explanation: Writes and reads a UTF-8 note using a temporary file.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.nio.file.Path p = java.nio.file.Files.createTempFile("note", ".txt"); try { java.nio.file.Files.writeString(p, "First"); java.nio.file.Files.writeString(p, "\nSecond", java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption.APPEND); System.out.println(java.nio.file.Files.readString(p)); } finally { java.nio.file.Files.deleteIfExists(p); } } }
examples.explanation: Appends text without replacing the existing note.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.nio.file.Path p = java.nio.file.Files.createTempFile("note", ".txt"); try { java.nio.file.Files.writeString(p, "A\nB\nC"); System.out.println(java.nio.file.Files.readAllLines(p).size()); } finally { java.nio.file.Files.deleteIfExists(p); } } }
examples.explanation: Counts note lines by reading them as a list.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name()); } }
examples.explanation: Names the explicit character encoding used for portable notes.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.nio.file.Path p = java.nio.file.Files.createTempFile("note", ".txt"); try { System.out.println(java.nio.file.Files.exists(p)); } finally { java.nio.file.Files.deleteIfExists(p); } } }
examples.explanation: Checks whether a saved note path exists and cleans up the temporary test file.

practise.guidedTask: Create a notes file under a temporary application directory. Write a note in UTF-8, append a second line, read it back and delete the temporary file in a finally block or try-with-resources design.
practise.independentTask: Implement a PersistentNotes class with create, append, list and delete operations. Keep path handling inside the class and report missing files clearly.
hints: Use a dedicated application data directory and validate IDs before resolving a path.
Specify UTF-8 explicitly and distinguish replace from append operations.
Test Unicode, empty and missing notes, path traversal attempts and cleanup after an I/O failure.
practise.challenge: Test Unicode text, an empty note, a missing file, append to an existing file and cleanup after an IOException.
